title: Abdominal Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with the classic triad of diverticulitis: LLQ pain, low-grade fever, and leukocytosis. He has changes in bowel habits with nausea and vomiting. He meets SIRS criteria (fever >100.4°F, WBC >12,000). CT abdomen/pelvis with IV and oral contrast is the gold standard — findings include bowel wall thickening, pericolic fat stranding, and a 2 cm abscess (complicated diverticulitis). Abscesses <3-4 cm can be managed conservatively with antibiotics alone without percutaneous drainage. Colonoscopy and barium enema are CONTRAINDICATED in acute diverticulitis due to risk of perforation. Treatment: NPO for bowel rest, IV fluids, IV antibiotics (cefazolin + metronidazole, cefuroxime + metronidazole, ceftriaxone + metronidazole, or ampicillin/sulbactam). High-fiber diet at discharge for prevention.

physical_exam.abdominal: LLQ tenderness. Assess for peritoneal signs, guarding, rebound.

decoys.label: Colonoscopy / Barium enema
decoys.reason_wrong: ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED in acute diverticulitis. Risk of bowel perforation from inflamed, friable tissue. Colonoscopy only after diverticulitis completely resolves (to rule out malignancy).

decoys.label: Percutaneous drainage for 2 cm abscess
decoys.reason_wrong: Abscesses <3-4 cm can be managed with antibiotics alone. Drainage indicated for abscesses >4 cm.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: CT with IV and oral contrast is definitive. Findings: bowel wall thickening, pericolic fat stranding, diverticula. Complicated: abscess, fistula, obstruction, perforation.

teach_me_steps.order: NPO + IV fluids for bowel rest
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Bowel rest is essential. IV fluids maintain hydration in NPO patient with nausea/vomiting.
Ceftriaxone + Metronidazole or Pip-Tazo or Ampicillin-Sulbactam. Small abscess <3-4 cm = antibiotics alone.

teach_me_steps.order: NEVER scope or use barium in acute setting
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Colonoscopy and barium enema risk perforation. Only after diverticulitis fully resolves to rule out malignancy.

case_summary: Complicated acute diverticulitis with 2 cm abscess. LLQ pain + fever + leukocytosis (SIRS). CT confirms. NPO + IV fluids + IV ceftriaxone/metronidazole. No drainage needed (<3-4 cm). Avoid colonoscopy. High-fiber diet at discharge.
